advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Force a C/POSIX locale (LC_ALL=C) for the merge whose output `_untracked_overwrite_paths` parses, or parse a locale-stable signal, so recovery is not defeated by the host locale.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:233: `marker = "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge"`
gitutil.run_git runs subprocess with env=None (inherits environment): src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:96 `return subprocess.run(argv,...env=env,...)` with env defaulting to None
No LC_ALL/LANG pinning in sync.py or gitutil.py (searched: quotepath none; LC_ALL only in integration tests)
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:244: `paths.append(stripped)` — the stripped line is used verbatim as a repo-relative path
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:263-265: `src = tracker_root / rel; if not src.exists(): return False`
No `-c core.quotepath=false` passed to the merge and no quotepath config found (search_files quotepath: no matches)
advisory.finding: `_untracked_overwrite_paths` matches an English-only marker ('untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge') and the trailer strings ('Please move or remove'/'Aborting'); git localizes these messages per LANG/LC_ALL, and `_git`/`run_git` inherit the ambient environment (env=None). Under a non-English locale the marker never matches, so recovery silently never triggers and the store wedges exactly as before.
merged_from: With core.quotepath at its default (true), git C-quotes and double-quotes untracked paths containing non-ASCII or special bytes in the 'would be overwritten' listing (e.g. `"dir/\303\251.json"`). `_untracked_overwrite_paths` returns the raw quoted/escaped line, and `_quarantine_untracked` then computes `src = tracker_root / rel` which will not exist, returning False. Recovery aborts silently for any such path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Run the union merge with env forcing LC_ALL=C / LANG=C (or GIT_* equivalents) before parsing its stderr, so the marker and path lines are stable.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_quarantine_untracked` all-or-nothing: validate every `src` exists before moving any, or roll back already-moved paths when a later path is missing.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:262-268: loop `for rel in paths:` does `shutil.move(...)` per iteration and `if not src.exists(): return False` mid-loop
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:203-217: caller uses the bool return but does not restore already-moved files on False
Docstring claims all-or-nothing: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:251 `Returns True only if every path was moved`
advisory.finding: `_quarantine_untracked` moves paths sequentially and returns False on the first path whose `src` does not exist, but any earlier paths in the list have ALREADY been `shutil.move`d out of the worktree. On that early-return the caller treats recovery as failed and falls to abort-only/keep-local, yet the worktree has been mutated (some untracked leftovers relocated) — contradicting the stated 'any other failure keeps today's abort-only behavior exactly' contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop or comment the pre-quarantine `git merge --abort` at sync.py:204 (the untracked-overwrite abort leaves no merge in progress).
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:204: `_git(tracker, "merge", "--abort")` inside `if leftovers:` before quarantine
The 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' error is git's pre-merge worktree check; no MERGE_HEAD is created, so no merge is in progress to abort
advisory.finding: The first `_git(tracker, "merge", "--abort")` at line 204 runs in response to the untracked-overwrite abort, but git raises that error as a pre-merge safety check with NO merge started, so there is nothing to abort — `git merge --abort` returns non-zero ('fatal: There is no merge to abort'). The result is discarded so it is harmless, but it is a guaranteed misleading no-op.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the redundant first `origin_sha` assignment (lines 161-164) in test_store_sync_reconverge.py, keeping only the `rev-parse HEAD` capture.
evidence:
tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py:161-165: `origin_sha = (
 _git(origin, "commit", ...) or _git(origin, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()
 )
 origin_sha = _git(origin, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()`
advisory.finding: In the genuine-conflict test, `origin_sha` is assigned twice with the first assignment being dead/confused: `origin_sha = (_git(origin, "commit", ...) or _git(origin, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip())` yields a CompletedProcess (truthy) or a str, then line 165 immediately overwrites it with the correct sha.
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete the first assignment block and keep `origin_sha = _git(origin, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where quarantine succeeds but the retried merge still fails (mixed untracked collision + tracked conflict), asserting clean abort and local kept.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:215 `if retry.returncode == 0:`
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:217 `merge = retry  # fall through to the abort-only net below`
ABSENCE: all three tests either self-heal on the first retry or never reach quarantine (genuine content conflict). None constructs a case where quarantine succeeds yet the retry merge still fails.
advisory.finding: The post-quarantine retry-failure fall-through (retry.returncode != 0 → merge = retry → abort-only net) has no test. After a successful quarantine, if the retried merge still fails for some other reason, the code must abort cleanly and keep local; no test drives a quarantine that succeeds followed by a still-failing retry.
scenarios: Origin introduces both an untracked-overwrite collision AND a tracked-content conflict, so the retry after quarantine still aborts.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a git-named untracked path is absent on disk so _quarantine_untracked returns False, asserting no retry and abort-only behavior with no data loss.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:262-265 `for rel in paths: src = tracker_root / rel; if not src.exists(): return False`
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:253-255 `common = ...; if not common: return False`
ABSENCE: no test drives _quarantine_untracked to return False; the collision fixture always makes the leftover exist on disk.
advisory.finding: _quarantine_untracked's False-return path (a git-named path not present on disk → return False, no retry) is untested. The contract 'a mis-identified file must stay recoverable' and the fall-through to abort-only when quarantine cannot complete are only asserted implicitly by never being exercised.
scenarios: git names a path that no longer exists on disk by the time quarantine runs; an already-partially-moved set on retry.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct unit test of _untracked_overwrite_paths on a synthetic multi-path merge output (with the 'Please move or remove'/'Aborting' trailer), asserting exactly the intended paths are returned.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:238-244 loop with `if stripped.startswith("Please move or remove") or stripped == "Aborting": break`
tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py:46-48 single `_COLLIDE_PATH` only
ABSENCE: no test provides a merge output with two or more untracked paths, nor asserts the trailer lines are excluded from the returned path list.
advisory.finding: The multi-path / trailer-boundary parsing in _untracked_overwrite_paths is untested. The happy-path fixture triggers exactly one colliding path, so the loop over multiple indented lines and the 'Please move or remove'/'Aborting' break conditions (which fence which lines are treated as paths) are never traversed. A parser bug that grabbed the trailer line as a path, or dropped/mis-split multiple paths, would pass all current tests.
scenarios: A compaction leaves multiple untracked leftovers (SNAPSHOT + .retired) all colliding with origin; git lists several paths followed by the trailer.
